method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Usually self-limiting in immunocompetent children — symptomatic treatment only.**
claims.source_text: Chickenpox is usually a self-limiting disease in immunocompetent children, requiring symptomatic treatment only
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Short prodrome** (fever, lethargy, anorexia), then rash over 3–5 days: **crops of papules → vesicles → crusts**, usually fully crusted by 10 days.
claims.source_text: Short prodrome of fever, lethargy and anorexia followed by eruption of rash over next 3-5 days … Crops of small papules, quickly become vesicular and then crust over after vesicles have ruptured Usually fully crusted over by 10 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Surrounding erythema is normal**, especially as lesions crust — **cellulitis tends to be over-diagnosed.**
claims.source_text: Lesions normally have significant surrounding erythema, particularly as they crust over - cellulitis tends to be over-diagnosed
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vaccinated children can still get chickenpox, but it is typically mild**; the vaccine itself may cause a rash 1–3 weeks later.
claims.source_text: Vaccine may cause a rash, typically 1-3 weeks later Children who are immunised may still become infected with VZV, but the disease is typically mild
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Complications:** bacterial superinfection (especially GAS and *S. aureus*), pneumonia, encephalitis, hepatitis, arthritis, Reye syndrome — **more common in premature neonates, neonates exposed before 7 days of age, unimmunised adolescents and the immunocompromised.**
claims.source_text: Complications include bacterial superinfection, particularly group A Streptococcus (GAS) and S aureus, pneumonia, encephalitis, hepatitis, arthritis and Reye syndrome … Complications are more common in premature neonates and neonates exposed before 7 days of age, unimmunised adolescents and immunocompromised children
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **At risk of complications:** malignancy · chemotherapy or high-dose steroids (over 20 mg/day prednisolone equivalent for 2 weeks) · immunodeficiency.
claims.source_text: Children at risk of complications Malignancy Receiving chemotherapy or high dose steroids (>20 mg/day prednisolone equivalent for 2 weeks) Immunodeficiency
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infectious from 2 days before the rash until the vesicles crust.** Exposed children are potentially infectious from day 8 to 21 after exposure (8–28 if they received VZIG).
claims.source_text: Children with chickenpox are infectious from 2 days before the appearance of rash until the vesicles are crusted over … Exposed children should be considered infectious from 8-21 days post exposure, or 8-28 days if they have received Varicella Zoster Immunoglobulin (VZIG)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Clinical diagnosis — no routine investigations.** In neonates or immunocompromised children a vesicle swab for VZV PCR may help.
claims.source_text: Chickenpox is a clinical diagnosis. No investigations are routinely required … In neonates or immunocompromised children, vesicular swab for VZV PCR may be helpful to confirm the diagnosis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Immunocompetent children over 1 week and under 12 years: no specific therapy.**
claims.source_text: In immunocompetent children >1 week old and <12 years old, no specific therapy is indicated
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid aspirin** (Reye syndrome) **and avoid NSAIDs** (invasive GAS).
claims.source_text: Avoid aspirin due to increased susceptibility to Reye syndrome … Avoid NSAIDs due to increased risk of invasive GAS
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Continue eczema treatment, including topical steroids.**
claims.source_text: For underlying eczema, continue eczema treatment including topical steroids
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider IV aciclovir for:** premature neonates and term neonates under 7 days of age · children at risk of, or with, complications.
claims.source_text: Consider IV aciclovir in the following cases Premature neonates and term neonates <7 days of age (see neonatal section) Children at risk of complications or with complications (see Assessment)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider oral aciclovir for:** unvaccinated children over 12 years · severe eczema · chronic pulmonary disease · salicylate therapy · oral steroid therapy · secondary household cases (usually more severe).
claims.source_text: Consider oral aciclovir in the following cases Unvaccinated child age >12 years Severe eczema Chronic pulmonary disease Children on salicylate therapy Children on oral steroid therapy Secondary cases in household contacts, as these are usually more severe
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Exclude from school, kindergarten and childcare until all lesions have crusted.** Avoid admission where possible; if admitted, isolate with contact precautions.
claims.source_text: Children must be excluded from school/kindergarten/childcare until all lesions crusted over … Avoid hospitalisation where possible. If required, isolation and contact precautions apply
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A pregnant woman exposed to chickenpox must be reviewed within 24 hours**, at any stage of pregnancy.
claims.source_text: Pregnant women who have had contact with chickenpox should be reviewed within 24 hours, regardless of the stage of pregnancy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Contacts aged 1 month–1 year:** observe if not at risk; **consider VZIG if at risk of complications.**
claims.source_text: Age 1 month-1 year: if not at risk of complications, observation is recommended. If at risk of complications (see Assessment), consider VZIG
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Contacts over 1 year: give VZV vaccine within 5 days of exposure** if no contraindication; if they cannot be vaccinated and are at risk, consider VZIG. A second vaccine dose does no harm if status is uncertain.
claims.source_text: Age >1 year: if within 5 days of exposure and no contraindications to vaccine, give VZV vaccine … There is no harm in having a second dose of VZV vaccine if immunisation status is uncertain or parents request this … If children are unable to have the vaccine and are at risk of complications, consider VZIG
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Immunodeficient contacts should receive VZIG**; their susceptible household contacts should receive VZV vaccine.
claims.source_text: Immunodeficient contacts should receive VZIG, and their household contacts should receive VZV vaccine if they are susceptible to disease
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Term neonate under 1 week with a chickenpox-like rash: investigate and treat with IV aciclovir.** Any exposed neonate who becomes unwell starts IV aciclovir, **whether or not VZIG was given.**
claims.source_text: If a term neonate <1 week of age develops a rash consistent with chicken pox, they should be investigated and treated with IV aciclovir … Neonates who have had an exposure to VZV and subsequently become unwell, regardless of whether they received VZIG, should be commenced on IV aciclovir
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **VZIG for an infant whose mother develops chickenpox from 7 days before to 2 days after delivery.** Maternal chickenpox, **born before 28 weeks** (no antibody transfer): VZIG. **Born after 28 weeks:** observe if maternal antibody present, VZIG if absent.
claims.source_text: Varicella Zoster Immune Globulin (VZIG) should be given to an infant whose mother develops chickenpox 7 days before to 2 days after delivery … Maternal chickenpox: born before 28 weeks No Ab transfer prior to delivery VZIG Maternal chickenpox: born after 28 weeks Maternal Ab present Observe Maternal Ab absent VZIG
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Exposure under 1 week of age:** from the mother — assume no maternal antibody, give VZIG; from someone else — observe if maternal antibody present, VZIG if absent. **If maternal serology is unknown, assume antibodies absent.**
claims.source_text: Age <1 week at exposure (exposed from mother) Assume Maternal Ab absent VZIG Age <1 week at exposure (exposed from contact other than mother) Maternal Ab present Observe Maternal Ab absent VZIG … If maternal serology is unknown, assume maternal antibodies absent
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Isolate an exposed hospitalised neonate for the first 21 days of life** (28 if VZIG given); exclude possibly exposed visitors from the nursery during days 8–21.
claims.source_text: Isolate a neonate who has had contact with VZV for the first 21 days of life (or 28 days if VZIG has been given) … Other visitors who may have been exposed should be excluded from the nursery during the infectious period (8-21 days)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maternal varicella does not prevent breastfeeding**; cover any breast lesions with gauze and an occlusive dressing.
claims.source_text: Maternal varicella is not a contraindication to breastfeeding. If the mother has lesions on her breasts, they should be covered with gauze and occlusive dressing
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **VZIG IM by weight:** 0–10 kg 200 IU (1 vial) · 11–30 kg 400 IU (2 vials) · over 30 kg 600 IU (3 vials). This deliberately differs from the product information, to minimise wastage.
claims.source_text: Varicella Zoster Immune Globulin (VZIG) Doses are given IM according to the following table Weight of patient (kg) Dose (IU) 0-10 200 (1 vial) 11-30 400 (2 vials) over 30 600 (3 vials) … The dose of VZIG recommended in the table differs from that in the product information to minimise wastage
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give VZIG within 96 hours of exposure** — it can still work up to 10 days. Normal human immunoglobulin can be used if VZIG is unavailable.
claims.source_text: VZIG should be administered within 96 hours of exposure but can be effective if administered up to 10 days following exposure … Normal human immunoglobulin can be used for the prevention of varicella if VZIG is unavailable
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss every child who meets criteria for IV aciclovir or VZIG with the paediatric team.**
claims.source_text: Any child meeting criteria for treatment with IV aciclovir or VZIG should be discussed with the local paediatric team
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Chickenpox (varicella)' (Last Updated July 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Chickenpox_varicella/, retrieved 2026-09-23
